summary: Russian forces continued long-range strikes across multiple Ukrainian oblasts overnight, with ballistic missiles, Shahed-type drones, and 'banderol' cruise missiles targeting Kyiv, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, Sumy, and Poltava regions. Ukrainian drone strikes hit the Afipsky oil refinery in Krasnodar Krai — the fifth such attack in 2026 — and a mysterious fire broke out at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex's pyrolysis unit. The EU approved a €6.1 billion military aid package for Ukraine timed to Independence Day, drawn from a previously approved €90 billion loan.
key_points: Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Afipsky oil refinery in Krasnodar Krai, with debris killing two and injuring two at the nearby Afipskaya railway station and damaging at least 10 houses. (Source: @eRadarrua/107029, @ukr_leaks_eng/32720)

A pyrolysis unit with 2.7 million tons/year projected capacity spontaneously ignited and burned at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex in Amur Oblast, forcing equipment shutdown and personnel evacuation. (Source: @eRadarrua/107031)

The EU approved a €6.1 billion military aid package for Ukraine for Independence Day, drawn from a previously approved €90 billion loan, earmarked for air/missile defense, missiles, ammunition, and radars. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32697)

Russian 145th motorized infantry battalion of the 'North' group advanced and expelled the Ukrainian 5th separate mechanized brigade from Novokonstantinovka in Sumy Oblast, with fighting ongoing. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32720)

Russia's 'Center' group liberated Kucherov Yar in DPR between Druzhkovka and Dobropolye, and the 'Vostok' group's 394th motorized infantry regiment liberated Dolynka in Zaporizhzhia Oblast. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32720)

Massive overnight Russian drone and missile barrages hit Kyiv, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa, Sumy, Poltava, Chernihiv, Mykolaiv, and Kharkiv oblasts, with ballistic missiles fired at Kremenchuk and 'banderol' cruise missiles striking multiple cities. (Source: @eRadarrua/107037, @mon1tor_ua/70969, @UkraineNow/83661)

In Belgorod Oblast, three civilians were killed and at least four injured in 24 hours, including two men killed by an FPV drone strike on a car in Otradnoye and a UAV explosion in Tavrovo. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32720)

Russia's 'North' group reported advances on the outskirts of Kazachya Lopana in Kharkiv Oblast and captured one serviceman from Ukraine's 58th separate motorized infantry brigade, with heavy fighting in Vasylivka. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32720)

sections.executive_summary: Russia launched massive overnight strikes across Ukraine using ballistic missiles, Shahed-type drones, and 'banderol' cruise missiles targeting at least 10 oblasts. Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Afipsky oil refinery in Krasnodar Krai — the fifth such attack in 2026 — causing casualties and significant damage, while a separate mysterious fire engulfed a key pyrolysis unit at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex. The EU approved a €6.1 billion military aid package for Ukraine timed to Independence Day, drawn from a previously approved €90 billion loan, underscoring continued Western backing amid intensifying operations.

sections.threat_assessment: The tempo of long-range strikes by both sides is markedly elevated, with Russia deploying ballistic missiles, Shahed-type drones, and cruise missiles across at least 10 Ukrainian oblasts overnight while Ukraine conducts deep strikes into Krasnodar Krai. Ukrainian advances on the Afipsky oil refinery — the fifth attack in 2026 — and the simultaneous fire at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex's pyrolysis unit (2.7 million tons/year capacity) represent a significant degradation of Russian energy infrastructure. Ground operations are intensifying across Sumy, Kharkiv, and Zaporizhzhia oblasts, with Russian forces conducting limited but persistent advances and capturing personnel. The EU's €6.1 billion tranche underscores sustained Western commitment to Ukrainian air defense and ammunition resupply.
sections.regional_response: The EU's €6.1 billion military aid package approved for Ukraine's Independence Day signals continued and substantial Western military backing, though it is drawn from the previously approved €90 billion loan facility rather than constituting new funding. Romania has emerged as a key ammunition production hub, with the Arsenal Resita plant — operated by British-founded TOR International — now producing 25,000 155mm rounds and 20,000 propellant bags per month, supplying both Ukraine and Pentagon contractor Go2Weapons (€285 million contract for 120,000 M107 shells). TOR International is expanding with a Canadian branch for artillery ammunition and thermoplastic rocket fuel production, and collaborates with Turkish firm ADOR and Serbian companies FOCUS STRATEGIES and DefTech.
sections.intelligence_notes: The reported 'mysterious' fire at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex's pyrolysis unit, combined with the Afipsky refinery strike, may indicate either a coincidence of events or an unattributed Ukrainian action given the pattern of deep strikes into Russian territory. Zelensky's adviser 'Flash' Beskrestnov stated that all Russian Geran jet drones are now controlled by real-time operators, with more than half likely having target acquisition capability, rendering electronic warfare systems ineffective against them. The report that ground drones paraded on Khreshchatyk were not sent to the front because of Zelensky's event (per volunteer Maria Berlinskaya) suggests resource allocation constraints on unmanned systems. Reports of Munirawi sending two ballistic missiles toward Kremenchuk highlight the continuing ballistic missile threat to Poltava Oblast.
